title: Where Member Relief Is Taken Off an Insured Return Charge
content:
# Counter Card: Where Member Relief Is Taken Off an Insured Return Charge

On a work order of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service the relief a member is allowed against an insured return is taken off one part of the charge or off the whole of it, according to whether a member benefit has been drawn on the membership held with the Belrose Circle Membership Programme in the twelve months to the handling date.

| The membership records show | Where the relief is taken off |
|---|---|
| The membership stands active and a member benefit has been drawn in the twelve months to the handling date | off the whole charge once every step has been applied |
| The membership stands active and no member benefit has been drawn in that window | off the value step alone, the rest of the charge carrying its steps in full |
| Any other case | neither of these two ways of taking the relief off applies |

**In words.** Where the membership stands active and a member benefit has been drawn in the twelve months to the handling date, the relief is taken off the whole charge once every step has been applied. Where the membership stands active and no member benefit has been drawn in that window, the relief is taken off the value step alone and the rest of the charge carries its steps in full. In any other case neither of those two ways applies.

**Worked on hypothetical inputs.** Take a level rate of 40.00 USD, a value step of 45 percent, no other step bearing on the leg, and relief of 25 percent.

- Where a member benefit has been drawn in the window: the charge with the value step applied comes to 58.00 USD, and the relief is taken off the whole of it, leaving 43.50 USD.
- Where no member benefit has been drawn in that window: the relief is taken off the value step alone, so that step stands at 33.75 percent of the rate for this purpose, and the charge comes to 53.50 USD.
